verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission uses liquid hydrogen (LH2) as fuel and liquid oxygen (LOX) as an oxidizer to power its core stage and upper stage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fuel the SLS rocket’s core stage with liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen... filling the ICPS with liquid hydrogen'; R2: 'pumping more than 700,000 gallons... of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen into the Space Launch System rocket'; R3: 'liquid oxygen tank and liquid hydrogen tank... to power the four RS-25 engines'
verifications.reasoning: Refs directly support LH2/LOX for core stage; upper stage (ICPS) explicitly LH2 in R1, LOX implied as part of SLS fueling in R2.

verifications.claim: Liquid hydrogen (LH2) and liquid oxygen (LOX) power the four RS-25 engines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'liquid oxygen tank and liquid hydrogen tank hold a combined 733,000 gallons of propellant... to power the four RS-25 engines'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match attributing LH2/LOX to RS-25 engines.

verifications.claim: Over 700,000 gallons are loaded into the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'loaded more than 700,000 gallons of fuel into the... Space Launch System rocket'; R3: 'hold a combined 733,000 gallons of propellant'
verifications.reasoning: Exact quantity and attribution to SLS confirmed.

verifications.claim: Solid rocket boosters using polybutadiene acrylonitrile (PBAN) are used.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No mention of PBAN in any reference.

verifications.claim: Liquid hydrogen (fuel) and liquid oxygen (oxidizer) for the core stage are stored at extremely low cryogenic temperatures to power the main engines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '733,000 gallons of propellant super cooled to minus 423 degrees Fahrenheit to power the four RS-25 engines'; R1: 'core stage with liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for core stage LH2/LOX at cryogenic temps for main engines.

verifications.claim: The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'propellant loading operations for the rocket’s interim cryogenic propulsion stage (ICPS)... filling the ICPS with liquid hydrogen'; R2: 'liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen into the Space Launch System rocket'
verifications.reasoning: LH2 explicit for ICPS; LOX not specified for ICPS but part of overall SLS fueling.

verifications.claim: The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) propels the Orion spacecraft toward the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the upper stage boosted the Orion capsule... into a higher orbit around Earth'
verifications.reasoning: Upper stage boosts Orion to higher Earth orbit; lunar trajectory by Orion engine, not explicit propulsion to Moon.

verifications.claim: The two strap-on solid rocket boosters use polybutadiene acrylonitrile (PBAN) combined with ammonium perchlorate.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No mention of PBAN or ammonium perchlorate.

verifications.claim: Cryogenic propellants must be constantly replenished during the countdown due to evaporation.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'teams continue to fuel the SLS rocket’s core stage with liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen... core stage liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen tanks... are currently in fast fill'
verifications.reasoning: Ongoing fueling ('continue', 'fast fill') implied for cryogenics, but no explicit mention of replenishment due to evaporation.
